The '''2026 VFL season''' was the 144th season of the [[Victorian Football League]] (VFL), a second-tier [[Australian rules football]] competition played in the states of [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]], [[New South Wales]], [[Queensland]] and [[Tasmania]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ralphsmith |first1=Jonty |title=VFL 2026 season dates locked in as VFLW campaign moved |url=https://www.zerohanger.com/vfl-2026-season-dates-locked-in-as-vflw-campaign-moved-171334/ |publisher=ZeroHanger |access-date=30 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251130090853/https://www.zerohanger.com/vfl-2026-season-dates-locked-in-as-vflw-campaign-moved-171334/ |archive-date=30 November 2025 |date=27 November 2025}}</ref> The season commenced on 20 March and concluded on 20 September.<ref name="afl27nov">{{cite web |title=2026 VFL and VFLW season dates |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/1457481/2026-vfl-and-vflw-season-dates |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=27 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251127145330/https://www.afl.com.au/news/1457481/2026-vfl-and-vflw-season-dates |archive-date=27 November 2025 |date=27 November 2025}}</ref>

{{VFL Box}} won the [[List of VFA/VFL premiers|premiership]] for the fourth time, defeating {{VFL Gee}} by 23 points in the [[#Grand Final|2026 VFL Grand Final]]. It was the first grand final since [[2019 VFL season|2019]] to feature two Victorian teams.

==Background==
===Broadcast rights===
The [[Seven Network]], which had broadcast VFL matches since [[2015 VFL season|2015]], did not renew its deal, stating that the practice was no longer commercially viable.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Knox |first1=David |title=Seven drops "not commercially viable" VFL |url=https://tvtonight.com.au/2026/01/seven-drops-not-commercially-viable-vfl.html |publisher=TV Tonight |access-date=15 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215091603/https://tvtonight.com.au/2026/01/seven-drops-not-commercially-viable-vfl.html |archive-date=15 February 2026 |date=28 January 2026}}</ref> During the [[2025 VFL season|2025 season]], one match per round had been shown in Victoria on its secondary channel, [[7mate]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Saturday night lights to shine on VFL |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/1281872/saturday-night-lights-to-shine-on-vfl |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=17 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317003443/https://www.afl.com.au/news/1281872/saturday-night-lights-to-shine-on-vfl |archive-date=17 March 2025 |date=17 March 2025}}</ref> On 12 February 2026, ''[[Crikey]]'' reported that the [[ABC Sport|ABC]] had secured the VFL television and radio rights for the 2026 season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Saeed |first1=Daanyal |title=ABC secures television and radio rights for the VFL |url=https://www.crikey.com.au/2026/02/12/vfl-on-abc-tv-radio-rights-2026/ |publisher=Crikey |access-date=15 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215091645/https://www.crikey.com.au/2026/02/12/vfl-on-abc-tv-radio-rights-2026/ |archive-date=15 February 2026 |date=12 February 2026}}</ref> The full broadcast deal was announced on 12 March 2026.<ref name="deal">{{cite web |title=Expanded VFL broadcast deal announced |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/1476113/expanded-vfl-broadcast-deal-announced |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=11 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311223823/https://www.afl.com.au/news/1476113/expanded-vfl-broadcast-deal-announced |archive-date=11 March 2026 |date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

The ABC broadcast one match per round, generally commencing at 12:05pm on Saturdays, which was available on [[ABC Victoria|ABC Television in Victoria]], [[ABC iview]] nationally, and simulcast on [[ABC Radio (Australia)|ABC Radio]] and [[ABC Listen]].<ref name="deal"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Jason Bennett returns to VFL coverage with the ABC after television and radio deal struck |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-03-12/jason-bennett-joins-the-abc-to-cover-the-vfl/106444476 |publisher=ABC News |access-date=11 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311224450/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-03-12/jason-bennett-joins-the-abc-to-cover-the-vfl/106444476 |archive-date=11 March 2026 |date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

[[Kayo Sports]], which previously broadcast VFL matches in [[2021 VFL season|2021]], streamed at least one home-and-away match per round (which was also shown on [[Fox Footy]]).<ref name="deal"/> The Seven Network broadcast all ten of the [[Tasmania Football Club]]'s home matches on [[TNT (Australian TV station)|Seven Tasmania]] and [[7plus]] nationally.<ref name="sen">{{cite web |title=SEN and SEG lock in historic Tassie Devils VFL deal |url=https://www.sen.com.au/news/2026/03/11/vfl-broadcast-deal-sen-tassie-devils |publisher=SEN |access-date=11 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311224430/https://www.sen.com.au/news/2026/03/11/vfl-broadcast-deal-sen-tassie-devils |archive-date=11 March 2026 |date=11 March 2026}}</ref> The [[Sports Entertainment Network]] (SEN) broadcast all of Tasmania's home-and-away matches on radio.<ref name="sen"/>

The preliminary finals and grand final were broadcast by the ABC.<ref name="deal"/> All matches continued to be broadcast online through the AFL's website and app.<ref name="deal"/>

==League membership==
In 2026, 22 teams competed in the VFL, the equal-most (with [[2021 VFL season|2021]]) to contest a VFA/VFL premiership in a single division.<ref name="fixture2026">{{cite web |title=2026 Smithy's VFL and VFLW fixtures confirmed |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/1464390/2026-smithys-vfl-and-vflw-fixtures-confirmed |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=15 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215092235/https://www.afl.com.au/news/1464390/2026-smithys-vfl-and-vflw-fixtures-confirmed |archive-date=15 February 2026 |date=11 February 2026}}</ref> It was the first time that clubs from four different states were represented in the same season.<ref name="fixture2026"/>

===Preston===
[[File:PCO_8.jpg|thumb|230px|Torn-down advertising signage next to a [[Preston Football Club]] banner at [[Preston City Oval]] in November 2025]]
The [[Preston Football Club|Northern Bullants]] faced several challenges throughout the [[2025 VFL season|2025 season]]. A new president and board took over in May 2025, reverting the club to its traditional "[[Preston Football Club]]" name on 20 August 2025, immediately after the conclusion of the home-and-away season.<ref>{{cite web |title='Time for action': Bullants need your support as club returns to Preston name |url=https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/time-for-action-bullants-need-your-support-as-club-returns-to-preston-name |publisher=Preston Football Club |access-date=13 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260218012327/https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/time-for-action-bullants-need-your-support-as-club-returns-to-preston-name |archive-date=18 February 2026 |date=20 August 2025}}</ref> The club had last competed as Preston in [[1999 VFL season|1999]] (when it was nicknamed the "Knights").<ref>{{cite web |title=Preston Football Club |url=https://libraries.darebin.vic.gov.au/Darebinheritage/sport-leisure/football/prestonfootballclub |publisher=Darebin Libraries |access-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116043814/https://libraries.darebin.vic.gov.au/Darebinheritage/sport-leisure/football/prestonfootballclub |archive-date=16 November 2025}}</ref>

At the same time, it was reported that the club could be in danger of folding because of debt, with the club asking the [[Australian Football League]] (AFL) to financially assist.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Amy |first1=Paul |last2=Michell |first2=Tim |title=Northern Bullants on brink of collapse after plea to AFL for debt bailout |url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/afl/northern-bullants-on-brink-of-collapse-after-plea-to-afl-for-debt-bailout/news-story/7d554cf9175c412a7a57dd7b5a811bd6 |publisher=Herald Sun |access-date=30 August 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250819063742/https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/afl/northern-bullants-on-brink-of-collapse-after-plea-to-afl-for-debt-bailout/news-story/7d554cf9175c412a7a57dd7b5a811bd6?amp |archive-date=19 August 2025 |date=19 August 2025}}</ref> On 6 October 2025, after years of uncompetitive performances, having struggled to pay its players and staff in 2025, and with questions over its long-term viability without the annual subsidies that clubs had received from the league prior to the pandemic-interrupted [[2020 VFL season|2020 season]], the VFL revoked the club's licence.<ref>{{cite web |title=Historic VFL club stripped of licence after 143 years of history as AFL makes call on debt crisis |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/afl/afl-2025-preston-football-club-loses-vfl-licence-after-143-years-of-history-northern-bullants-debt-carlton-blues-affiliation-latest-news/news-story/6a94dc518bb3d5269378597a45fbaa51 |publisher=Fox Sports |access-date=13 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211222304/https://www.foxsports.com.au/afl/afl-2025-preston-football-club-loses-vfl-licence-after-143-years-of-history-northern-bullants-debt-carlton-blues-affiliation-latest-news/news-story/6a94dc518bb3d5269378597a45fbaa51 |archive-date=11 December 2025 |date=6 October 2025}}</ref>

It was the not the first time Preston's history that it had faced similar circumstances – in [[1912 VFA season|1912]] it amalgamated with {{VFA Nor}}, in [[1997 VFL season|1997]] its licence was withdrawn but was restored after one month, and in [[2020 VFL season|2020]] it almost folded after {{AFL Car}} ended their [[Australian Football League reserves affiliations|affiliation]].<ref>{{cite web |title='Time for action': Bullants need your support as club returns to Preston name |url=https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/time-for-action-bullants-need-your-support-as-club-returns-to-preston-name |publisher=Preston Football Club |access-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116043923/https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/time-for-action-bullants-need-your-support-as-club-returns-to-preston-name |archive-date=16 November 2025 |date=20 August 2025}}</ref>

Initially, Preston club officials expressed optimism about regaining a VFL licence in 2027 or 2028.<ref>{{cite web |title=Proud to be Preston: Three Clubs. United. One Jumper. |url=https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/proud-to-be-preston-three-clubs-united-one-jumper |publisher=Preston Football Club |access-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116043943/https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/proud-to-be-preston-three-clubs-united-one-jumper |archive-date=16 November 2025 |date=22 October 2025}}</ref> However, faced with no viable path to readmission, the club entered voluntary liquidation after a meeting of members on 15 December 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Club statement |url=https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/club-statement-2 |publisher=Preston Football Club |access-date=31 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251231112502/https://www.prestonfc.com.au/post/club-statement-2 |archive-date=31 December 2025 |date=17 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Keating |first1=Mitch |title=Preston FC members vote on voluntary liquidation, Bullants to be deregistered |url=https://www.zerohanger.com/preston-fc-members-vote-on-voluntary-liquidation-bullants-to-be-deregistered-171808/ |publisher=ZeroHanger |access-date=28 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251222231558/https://www.zerohanger.com/preston-fc-members-vote-on-voluntary-liquidation-bullants-to-be-deregistered-171808/ |archive-date=22 December 2025 |date=17 December 2025}}</ref>

===St Kilda===
[[File:Trevor Barker Beach Oval 2026 24.jpg|thumb|230px|Promotional signage inside [[Trevor Barker Beach Oval]] for {{VFL San}}'s return as a standalone team]]
{{AFL|StK}} competed in the VFL with its own [[reserves team]] during the [[2000 VFL season|2000 season]], before entering into an [[Australian Football League reserves affiliations|affiliation]] with {{VFL SV}} (later renamed {{VFL Cas}}) in [[2001 VFL season|2001]]. The agreement ended after the [[2008 VFL season|2008 season]] and St Kilda affiliated with {{VFL San}} in [[2009 VFL season|2009]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Saints, Demons in VFL affiliate swap |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/102841/saints-demons-in-vfl-affiliate-swap |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116051549/https://www.afl.com.au/news/102841/saints-demons-in-vfl-affiliate-swap |archive-date=16 November 2025 |date=5 June 2008}}</ref>

In April 2025, Sandringham rejected a proposal from St Kilda to be renamed to the "Sandringham Saints" and move all home matches from [[Trevor Barker Beach Oval]] to [[Moorabbin Oval]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wu |first1=Andrew |last2=Spits |first2=Scott |title=Why the Saints could split from their VFL team; Sam Darcy avoids knee surgery |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/afl/wouldn-t-be-doing-the-right-thing-why-the-saints-could-split-from-their-vfl-team-20250424-p5lu12.html |publisher=Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116052010/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/afl/wouldn-t-be-doing-the-right-thing-why-the-saints-could-split-from-their-vfl-team-20250424-p5lu12.html |archive-date=16 November 2025 |date=24 April 2025}}</ref> The proposal also would have resulted in Sandringham permanently using St Kilda's colours of red, black and white (which it had already worn as an away jumper beginning in [[2019 VFL season|2019]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=Sandringham releases clash guernsey for 2019 |url=https://www.sandringhamfc.com.au/latest-news/sandringham-releases-clash-guernsey-for-2019 |publisher=Sandringham Football Club |access-date=19 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011225/https://www.sandringhamfc.com.au/latest-news/sandringham-releases-clash-guernsey-for-2019 |archive-date=13 April 2025 |date=8 April 2019}}</ref>

On 30 June 2025, St Kilda announced it would end its affiliation with Sandringham following the 2025 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=St Kilda to field standalone VFL team in 2026 |url=https://www.saints.com.au/news/1817429/vfl |publisher=St Kilda Football Club |access-date=30 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250630041810/https://www.saints.com.au/news/1817429/vfl |archive-date=30 June 2025 |date=30 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Keating |first1=Mitch |title=St Kilda make call on VFL team for 2026 |url=https://www.zerohanger.com/st-kilda-make-call-on-vfl-team-for-2026-164590/ |publisher=ZeroHanger |access-date=30 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250630041958/https://www.zerohanger.com/st-kilda-make-call-on-vfl-team-for-2026-164590/ |archive-date=30 June 2025 |date=30 June 2025}}</ref> The AFL granted a VFL licence to St Kilda the same day, while Sandringham continued in the competition as a standalone team.<ref>{{cite web |title=St Kilda approved VFL licence |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/1354925/st-kilda-approved-vfl-licence |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=30 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250630072728/https://www.afl.com.au/news/1354925/st-kilda-approved-vfl-licence |archive-date=30 June 2025 |date=30 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Alvaro |first1=Michael |title=Recruitment drive: Standalone Sandringham's signing spree |url=https://central.rookieme.com/afl/2026/01/22/recruitment-drive-standalone-sandringhams-signing-spree/ |publisher=Rookie Me Central |access-date=26 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260126144341/https://central.rookieme.com/afl/2026/01/22/recruitment-drive-standalone-sandringhams-signing-spree/ |archive-date=26 January 2026 |date=22 January 2026}}</ref>

Sandringham defeated {{VFL Wer}} in [[#Round 2|round 2]] after trailing by 34 points at half-time, which was its first victory as a standalone team since the [[1999 VFL season|1999 VFL semi-final]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ralphsmith |first1=Jonty |title=From the brink to a famous win: stand-alone Sandringham on the board |url=https://www.zerohanger.com/from-the-brink-to-a-famous-win-stand-alone-sandringham-on-the-board-174707/ |publisher=ZeroHanger |access-date=31 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260331041904/https://www.zerohanger.com/from-the-brink-to-a-famous-win-stand-alone-sandringham-on-the-board-174707/ |archive-date=31 March 2026 |date=29 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=McGuire |first1=Casey |title=VFL Match Report: Round 2 vs Werribee |url=https://www.sandringhamfc.com.au/latest-news/vfl-match-report-round-2-vs-werribee |publisher=Sandringham Football Club |access-date=31 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260331041751/https://www.sandringhamfc.com.au/latest-news/vfl-match-report-round-2-vs-werribee |archive-date=31 March 2026 |date=30 March 2026}}</ref>

===Tasmania===
[[File:WERvTAS2026PM 17.jpg|thumb|250px|{{AFL Tas}} during its first practice match against {{VFL Wer}} on 7 March 2026]]
On 5 September 2025, the [[Tasmania Football Club]] was granted a licence to compete in the VFL from 2026, ahead of its planned entry into the AFL from the 2028 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tasmania to enter VFL and VFLW in 2026 |url=https://www.afl.com.au/news/1411172/tasmania-to-enter-vfl-and-vflw-in-2026 |publisher=AFL.com.au |access-date=5 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250905041125/https://www.afl.com.au/news/1411172/tasmania-to-enter-vfl-and-vflw-in-2026 |archive-date=5 September 2025 |date=5 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Tasmania Football Club to Enter VFL and VFLW in 2026 |url=https://tasmaniafc.com/news/tasmania-football-club-to-enter-vfl-and-vflw-in-2026/ |publisher=Tasmania Football Club |access-date=5 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250905041642/https://tasmaniafc.com/news/tasmania-football-club-to-enter-vfl-and-vflw-in-2026/ |archive-date=5 September 2025 |date=5 September 2025}}</ref> [[Jeromey Webberley]] was appointed as the club's inaugural VFL coach, while former {{AFL Ess}} player [[Jye Menzie]] became the club's first player when he was signed on 30 September 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hann |first1=Ben |title=Tasmania Devils reveal inaugural coach after reaching massive milestone |url=https://www.examiner.com.au/story/9060249/tasmania-devils-appoint-first-vfl-coach-jeromey-webberley/ |publisher=The Examiner |access-date=8 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250908015523/https://www.examiner.com.au/story/9060249/tasmania-devils-appoint-first-vfl-coach-jeromey-webberley/ |archive-date=8 September 2025 |date=8 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Devils Sign First VFL Athlete |url=https://tasmaniafc.com/news/devils-sign-first-vfl-athlete/ |publisher=Tasmania Football Club |access-date=30 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930071658/https://tasmaniafc.com/news/devils-sign-first-vfl-athlete/ |archive-date=30 September 2025 |date=30 September 2025}}</ref>

Tasmania played its first official practice match against {{VFL Wer}} at [[RMIT Oval]] on 7 March 2026, losing 14.8 (92) to 10.12 (72).<ref>{{cite web |title=Promising Signs In Tasmania Practice Match Win |url=https://www.werribeefc.com.au/news/1257-promising-signs-in-tasmania-practice-match-win |publisher=Werribee Football Club |access-date=9 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260309123429/https://www.werribeefc.com.au/news/1257-promising-signs-in-tasmania-practice-match-win |archive-date=9 March 2026 |date=9 March 2026}}</ref> It played its first home-and-away season match against {{VFL Cob}} at [[North Hobart Oval]] in [[#Round 1|round 1]], winning 14.12 (96) to 11.13 (79).<ref>{{cite web |title=Tasmania Devils win historic first VFL clash |url=https://www.espn.com.au/afl/story/_/id/48265720/afl-tasmania-devils-win-historic-first-vfl-clash-beating-coburg |publisher=ESPN |access-date=21 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260321050314/https://www.espn.com.au/afl/story/_/id/48265720/afl-tasmania-devils-win-historic-first-vfl-clash-beating-coburg |archive-date=21 March 2026 |date=21 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="pulse28feb">{{cite web |title=North Hobart Oval capacity set at 11,135 for Tasmania Devils VFL return |url=https://pulsetasmania.com.au/news/north-hobart-oval-capacity-set-at-11135-for-tasmania-devils-return/ |publisher=Pulse Tasmania |access-date=28 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260228030421/https://pulsetasmania.com.au/news/north-hobart-oval-capacity-set-at-11135-for-tasmania-devils-return/ |archive-date=28 February 2026 |date=28 February 2026}}</ref>

It was the first time a club from [[Tasmania]] had competed in the VFL since the [[Tasmanian Devils (2001–2008)|original Tasmania Football Club]], which competed from [[2001 VFL season|2001]] until the end of [[2008 VFL season|2008]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Newlinds |first1=Peter |title=Tasmania gripped by footy fever |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2003-09-02/tasmania-gripped-by-footy-fever/1473468 |publisher=ABC News |access-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116054233/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2003-09-02/tasmania-gripped-by-footy-fever/1473468 |archive-date=16 November 2025 |date=2 September 2003}}</ref>

==Representative match==
An [[Interstate matches in Australian rules football|interstate representative match]] against the [[South Australian National Football League]] (SANFL) was again played during the AFL's [[Gather Round]], marking the third successive season the fixture was scheduled. The match was played at [[Glenelg Oval|Stratarama Stadium]], the home ground of [[Glenelg Football Club|Glenelg]], and was part of a double-header alongside a women's match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/afl/news/state-leagues-exhibition-games-set-afl-gather-round-2026-vfl-sanfl/afda5fa97995154a901bf8ec|title=State leagues exhibition games set for AFL Gather Round 2026|work=The Sporting News|date=10 December 2025|author=Jake Beddard|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251222063823/https://www.sportingnews.com/au/afl/news/state-leagues-exhibition-games-set-afl-gather-round-2026-vfl-sanfl/afda5fa97995154a901bf8ec|archive-date=22 December 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>
